mainTopic: טומאה of idol offerings; כלים of בית חוניו and the altar stones; who can nullify an idol
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a question about ביטול. Once an idol is nullified, its rabbinic טומאה clearly goes away too. But the איסור on a food offering to an idol can never be removed, as רב גידל taught, so the גמרא asks whether its rabbinic טומאה can still be cancelled. That question ends in תיקו. Next, רבי יוסי בן שאול asks רבי whether כלים used in בית חוניו may be used in the בית המקדש. רבי says they are forbidden, and the פסוק about King אחז's כלים turns out to be his forgotten source: the old כלים were put away and new ones were sanctified in their place. The גמרא then discusses the altar stones the Greeks defiled. רב פפא explains that those stones had already lost their holiness, and the גמרא explains that the חשמונאים stored them away because things used in holy service should not be put to ordinary use. A new משנה then teaches who can nullify an idol and how far ביטול reaches. רבי's two versions of the משנה are explained through an idol owned by a נכרי and a Jew together.

steps.title: No question about the idol itself
steps.stepSummary: For an idol that has been nullified, the טומאה clearly goes away together with the איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since its prohibition is nullified, its impurity is also nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation: there can be no question about the idol itself. Once its איסור is cancelled through ביטול, its טומאה is cancelled too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of עבודה זרה is rabbinic, and it is tied to the איסור. When the איסור is removed, there is no reason for the טומאה to stay. This narrows down where the real question must be.

phrases.english: Since its prohibition is nullified,
phrases.notes: "Its" means the idol itself, which was being discussed just before this.

phrases.english: the impurity is also nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section, ruling out the idol itself as the subject of the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For a nullified idol, the טומאה is clearly nullified along with the איסור, so the question cannot be about it.

steps.title: The real question: food offerings to an idol
steps.stepSummary: The question is really about a food offering to עבודה זרה. Its איסור never goes away, so does its rabbinic טומאה stay too, or can that be nullified?
steps.simpleTranslation: When he asked, it was about an offering of food to an idol: what is the law? Do we say that since its prohibition is never nullified (as רב גידל taught), its impurity also is never nullified? Or perhaps only the Torah-level prohibition stays, while the rabbinic-level impurity can be nullified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the question was really about: a food offering (תקרובת) brought to an idol. It then lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל teaches that the איסור of an idol offering can never be nullified. One side says the rabbinic טומאה follows the איסור and also stays. The other side says the two can split: the Torah איסור stays, but the rabbis' טומאה can go away.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to an idol
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different things are in play here: the איסור (forbidden to benefit from, Torah law) and the טומאה (impurity, rabbinic law). The question is whether they must always go together.

phrases.english: When he raises the question,

phrases.aramaic: תִּקְרוֹבֶת לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל אוֹכְלִין, מַאי?
phrases.english: it is about an offering of food to an idol: what is the law?
Since its prohibition is not nullified,
as רב גידל taught,
phrases.notes: רב גידל taught that the איסור on an offering to an idol can never be cancelled.

phrases.english: is the impurity also not nullified?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אִיסּוּר דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא בָּטֵיל,
phrases.english: Or perhaps the prohibition, which is from the Torah, is not nullified,
but the impurity, which is rabbinic, is nullified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled out the idol itself, moves the question to food offerings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rabbinic טומאה of a food offering to עבודה זרה stay permanently like its איסור, or can it be nullified?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about food offerings is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer. The question about the טומאה of food offerings stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found that decides between the two sides. Both possibilities remain on the table.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: For a nullified idol, the טומאה goes with the איסור. For a food offering, whose איסור is permanent, it is unresolved whether the rabbinic טומאה stays as well.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 2 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of whether the טומאה of a food offering can be nullified remains open.

steps.title: May vessels from בית חוניו be used in the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן שאול asks רבי whether כלים that were used in בית חוניו may later be used in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן שאול asked רבי: vessels that were used in בית חוניו, may they be used in the בית המקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It is about whether כלים used in another temple, בית חוניו, become unfit for use in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic, though it is still about whether something becomes disqualified through improper worship. The next steps will explain exactly what the question is.

keyTerms.meaning: The temple built by חוניו, outside ירושלים

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל מֵרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul asked Rabbi:
phrases.notes: "רבי" on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Vessels that were used in the temple of Onias,
may they be used in the Temple?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל מֵרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are כלים used in בית חוניו fit for use in the בית המקדש?

steps.title: The question assumes בית חוניו was not idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question only makes sense according to the view that בית חוניו was not a house of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked this according to the one who says that בית חוניו was not a temple of idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies the background of the question. If בית חוניו were idol worship, the כלים would obviously be forbidden, so the question must follow the view that it was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, בית חוניו served ה׳, but in the wrong place. That is what makes the question real: is serving there bad enough to disqualify the כלים?

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: And he raised this question
according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית חוֹנְיוֹ לָאו בֵּית עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא,
phrases.english: that the temple of Onias was not a temple of idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines which opinion the question in step 4 follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question follows the view that בית חוניו was not a house of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A משנה showing that view
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says כהנים who served in בית חוניו may not serve in the מקדש, and that this is all the more true of those who served idols. This shows בית חוניו was treated as something other than idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: כהנים who served in בית חוניו may not serve in the מקדש in ירושלים, and needless to say those who served 'something else' (idol worship).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source for the view that בית חוניו was not idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats idol worship as a separate, worse case ("needless to say"). So it must hold that בית חוניו itself was not idol worship. It also shows that כהנים who served there were penalized.

keyTerms.meaning: "Something else", a polite way of saying idol worship

phrases.english: As we learned: Priests who served in the temple of Onias
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מנחות 109a.

phrases.english: may not serve in the Temple in Jerusalem,
and needless to say, those who served something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view mentioned in step 5 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a view holding בית חוניו was not a house of עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מנחות, which treats serving "something else" (idols) as a separate, more obvious case.

steps.title: Are only כהנים penalized, or כלים too?
steps.stepSummary: The two sides of the question: maybe the rabbis penalized only כהנים, because they are responsible people, and not כלים. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only the כהנים that the rabbis penalized, because they are people with understanding, but not the vessels? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what רבי יוסי בן שאול was unsure about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty on the כהנים is a קנס, a rabbinic penalty. A קנס makes sense for people who chose to act, but כלים have no understanding. The question is whether the rabbis extended the קנס to objects anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: People with understanding, responsible for what they do

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a general question: does a rabbinic קנס apply only to responsible people, or also to the objects involved?

phrases.english: Is it the priests whom the Sages penalized,
because they are people with understanding,
but vessels, no?
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה about כהנים to set out both sides of the question about כלים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the קנס on כהנים who served in בית חוניו extend to the כלים used there?

steps.title: רבי rules the כלים are forbidden but has forgotten his source
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that the כלים of בית חוניו are forbidden. He once knew a פסוק that teaches this, but he has forgotten it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: They are forbidden. We had a פסוק that teaches this, but we forgot it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the question from Step 4: the כלים from בית חוניו may not be used in the מקדש. He admits he cannot remember the פסוק that is the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 7 was whether the penalty given to the כהנים also applies to כלים. רבי says yes: the כלים are forbidden too. His ruling has a scriptural source, but he cannot recall it, which sets up the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: They are forbidden,
phrases.notes: רבי is answering רבי יוסי בן שאול about the כלים of בית חוניו.

phrases.english: and we had a verse in our hands
phrases.notes: "In our hands" means we knew a פסוק that teaches this.

phrases.english: but we forgot it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question laid out in Steps 4 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כלים of בית חוניו may be used in the מקדש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are forbidden. There is a פסוק source, but it has been forgotten.

steps.title: Challenge from the פסוק about King אחז's כלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן שאול quotes a פסוק saying that the כלים King אחז had misused were "prepared and sanctified." This seems to mean they were purified and used again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: "All the כלים that King אחז cast away in his reign, in his unfaithfulness, we have prepared and sanctified." Doesn't "prepared" mean we immersed them in a מקוה, and "sanctified" mean we made them holy again for use?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן שאול challenges רבי with a פסוק. The פסוק seems to show that כלים used for עבודה זרה could be purified and returned to the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחז used the מקדש's כלים for idol worship. If the פסוק means those same כלים were immersed and sanctified again, then even כלים used for real עבודה זרה can return to service. By a קל וחומר, the כלים of בית חוניו, which was not עבודה זרה, should certainly be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: cast away, made disgusting (through idol worship)
that we immersed them (in a מקוה)

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי בן שאול is now challenging רבי.

phrases.english: "All the vessels that were cast away by
King Ahaz in his reign, in his treachery,
we have prepared and sanctified,"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 29:19

phrases.english: Is it not that "we prepared" means that we immersed them,
and "sanctified" means that we sanctified them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's ruling from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the כלים of בית חוניו are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to show that כלים used for real עבודה זרה were purified and reused. So the כלים of בית חוניו, which was less severe, should surely be allowed.

steps.title: רבי rereads the פסוק: the old כלים were put away and new ones were sanctified
steps.stepSummary: רבי thanks him for reminding him of his forgotten פסוק. He explains that "prepared" means the old כלים were stored away, and "sanctified" means new כלים were sanctified in their place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Blessed are you to Heaven, for you have returned my lost item to me. "We prepared" means we put them away. "We sanctified" means we sanctified other כלים in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the challenge by reading the פסוק differently. He says this is the very פסוק he had forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי's reading, the כלים of אחז were never reused. They were put away (גניזה), and new כלים replaced them. So the פסוק that seemed to challenge רבי is actually his source that misused כלים become forbidden for the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: that we put them away (stored them so they would not be used)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides read the very same פסוק. The disagreement is only about the meaning of "הכנו" and "הקדשנו": reusing the old כלים, or putting them away and sanctifying new ones.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's source is the פסוק about אחז: כלים that were misused were put away and replaced, not returned to the מקדש. So the כלים of בית חוניו are forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: Blessed are you to Heaven
for you have returned my lost item to me.
phrases.notes: The "lost item" is the פסוק רבי had forgotten in Step 8.

phrases.english: "We prepared" means that we put them away,
and "we sanctified" means that we sanctified others in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה לַשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁהֶחְזַרְתָּ לִי אֲבֵדָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9 and turns it into רבי's own source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Prepared and sanctified" means the same כלים were immersed and sanctified again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The old כלים were put away, and new כלים were sanctified in their place. Misused כלים may not return to the מקדש.

steps.title: Possible support from the altar stones the Greeks defiled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a support for רבי from a משנה. It says the חשמונאים put away the altar stones that the Greeks defiled, and רב ששת explains that they were defiled for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? In the northeastern room, the חשמונאים put away the altar stones that the Greeks defiled. And רב ששת said: They defiled them by using them for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a proof for רבי's view. Stones of the מזבח that were used for idol worship were put away, not reused. The word "לֵימָא" ("shall we say") signals that the גמרא is testing this proof. The next step examines it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the altar stones had to be put away after being used for עבודה זרה, this matches רבי's rule that misused כלים of the מקדש are forbidden. רב ששת's explanation matters because it shows the problem was specifically idol worship, not some other kind of defilement.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say this supports him
they put away (stored them so they would not be used)

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי. "לימא" hints that this proof might still be questioned.

phrases.english: The northeastern [room]
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting a משנה that describes rooms in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: in it the Hasmoneans put away
the stones of the altar
that the Greeks defiled,
And Rav Sheshet said:
that they defiled them for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי's ruling is defended, the גמרא looks for more support for it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's ruling that misused כלים of the מקדש are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the altar stones the Greeks defiled, which the חשמונאים put away, together with רב ששת's explanation that they were defiled for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The altar stones were a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof: a פסוק taught that the מזבח lost its holiness when the enemies entered, so it says nothing about holy כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There, they found a פסוק and learned from it, as it is written: 'And robbers shall enter into it and profane it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the proof for רבי from the חשמונאים's altar stones. He says that case was different because of a special פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the stones were still holy when the Greeks used them for idol worship, and still became forbidden. רב פפא says the פסוק teaches that when the 'robbers' entered, the מקדש became ordinary, non-holy property. So the stones were plain stones when they were worshipped, and that tells us nothing about holy כלים like those of בית חוניו.

keyTerms.meaning: he expounded, learned a lesson from it
and they will profane it, making it no longer holy

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the stones were permitted. He agrees they were forbidden. He is saying they became forbidden as ordinary stones, not as holy objects.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There, someone found a verse and expounded it,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the altar stones from the previous step.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"And robbers shall enter into it and profane it."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 7:22

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב פפא התם קרא אשכח ודרש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the altar stones to holy כלים used for עבודה זרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The altar stones had already lost their holiness, because of the פסוק, before they were worshipped.

steps.title: Why the stones had to be stored away
steps.stepSummary: The חשמונאים could not break the stones or saw them, so the only option left was to put them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What shall we do? Break them? The Torah says 'whole stones.' Saw them? The Torah says 'Do not lift iron upon them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חשמונאים put the stones away instead of fixing them. They could not break them, and they could not saw them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden stones could not stay in the מזבח. Breaking them would go against the rule that altar stones must be whole. Cutting them with iron is also forbidden for altar stones, so storing them away was the only option.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the Torah

phrases.english: They said: What shall we do?
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חשמונאים, figuring out what to do with the defiled stones.

phrases.english: Shall we break them?
"Whole stones," says the Merciful One!
phrases.notes: דברים 27:6

phrases.english: Shall we saw them?
"You shall not lift iron upon them," says the Merciful One.
phrases.notes: דברים 27:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the detail in the משנה that the stones were stored away
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The defiled altar stones could be neither broken nor sawed, so they had to be stored away.

steps.title: Why not break them and keep them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חשמונאים didn't break the stones and take them for private use. It starts to support this with a statement from רב אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let them break the stones and take them for themselves! Didn't רב אושעיא say: 'They wanted to store away all the silver and gold in the world because of the silver and gold of ירושלים'? And we asked: Is ירושלים most of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last step: the חשמונאים had another option. It begins bringing a source to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with breaking was only that broken stones cannot stay in the מזבח. Since the פסוק made them non-holy, why not break them and use them as ordinary stones? רב אושעיא's statement as first quoted was hard to understand, so the גמרא is about to bring the corrected version.

keyTerms.meaning: let them take them for themselves
to store away, put out of use
and we discussed it, asked about it

phrases.english: But why?
Let them break them and take them for themselves!
Didn't Rav Oshaya say:
"They wished to store away all the silver and gold in the world
because of the silver and gold of Jerusalem,"
phrases.notes: Much of ירושלים's wealth belonged to the מקדש and got mixed in with other money.

phrases.english: and we discussed it:
Is Jerusalem the majority of the world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 13 that storing away was the only option
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the חשמונאים had no choice but to store the stones away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stones were non-holy because of the פסוק, so breaking them for private use should have been allowed.

steps.title: אביי's version: the פסוק permitted the coins
steps.stepSummary: אביי corrects the statement: the חכמים wanted to store away worn coins of Hadrian and Trajan, until they found that the פסוק permits Temple wealth taken by enemies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: They wanted to store away the worn dinars of Hadrian and Trajan because of the coins of ירושלים, until they found a פסוק showing it is permitted: 'And robbers shall enter into it and profane it.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the corrected version of the story. It finishes the proof behind the challenge: the same פסוק makes Temple wealth taken by enemies permitted for ordinary use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern was limited to specific coins known to contain Temple gold and silver. The חכמים permitted them because of 'robbers shall enter it and profane it.' That same פסוק applies to the altar stones, so the question stands: why not break them and use them?
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'וּבָאוּ בָהּ פָּרִיצִים וְחִלְּלוּהָ' teaches that when enemies took over the מקדש, its holy property lost its holiness. This is why the altar stones prove nothing about holy כלים, and why the גמרא now asks why the stones weren't broken and used.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
They wished to store away
the worn-out dinars of Hadrian and Trajan,
because of the coins of Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: These coins were known to contain gold and silver taken from the מקדש.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמָּצְאוּ לָהּ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: until they found a verse from the Torah that it is permitted:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is really in יחזקאל. Here 'Torah' just means a verse from תנ"ך.

phrases.english: "And robbers shall enter into it and profane it!"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 7:22

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר אביי בקשו לגנוז דינרא הדריינא טוריינא שיפא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source quoted in the challenge of step 14
steps.raayaObject: That the altar stones, once broken, could have been used for ordinary purposes
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's version of רב אושעיא's statement: coins with Temple metal were permitted because of the פסוק in יחזקאל

steps.title: Coins never used for service, but altar stones were
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. The coins of ירושלים were never used in service of גבוה, but the altar stones were, so it is improper for an ordinary person to use them.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the coins were never used for the Most High. Here, the stones were used for the Most High, so it is not proper for an ordinary person to use them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the case of the coins does not prove that the חשמונאים could have used the stones privately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the coins and the stones lost their holiness when enemies took them. But the stones had actually served on the מזבח, while the coins were only set aside as holy. Something that was really used for holy service should not be turned into an everyday object, so the stones had to be put away.

keyTerms.meaning: The Most High: holy service to ה׳
An ordinary person, or ordinary everyday use
Proper conduct, the respectful way to act
There / here: the words used to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: Even after something holy loses its holiness, if it was actually used for holy service, we do not lower it to ordinary use. That is why the חשמונאים put the stones away.

phrases.english: There, they were not used for the Most High;
phrases.notes: "There" means the worn coins of Hadrian and Trajan from step 15.

phrases.english: here, since they were used for the Most High
phrases.notes: "Here" means the altar stones the חשמונאים put away.

phrases.english: it is not proper conduct
for an ordinary person to use them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by showing that the coin case from step 15 is different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since enemies remove holiness, the stones could have been broken up and used privately, just like the coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Items that were actually used in holy service should not be used for ordinary purposes, so the stones were put away.

steps.title: The משנה: who can nullify an idol, and its accessories
steps.stepSummary: A נכרי can nullify his own idol or another נכרי's, but a Jew cannot nullify a נכרי's idol. Nullifying the idol also nullifies its accessories, but nullifying only the accessories leaves the idol forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile can nullify his own idol and his friend's idol, but a Jew cannot nullify a gentile's idol. Whoever nullifies the idol nullifies its accessories too. If he nullified only the accessories, the accessories are permitted, but the idol is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the rules of ביטול: who can remove an idol's forbidden status, and how far that nullification reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a נכרי, who could own or worship the idol, has the power to nullify it. A Jew has no such power. Accessories depend on the idol, so they follow it, but the idol does not follow its accessories.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifies: removes an idol's forbidden status, for example by damaging it on purpose
Accessories used in serving the idol

steps.confusionAlert: Nullifying works one way only. Nullifying the idol frees its accessories, but nullifying the accessories does NOT free the idol.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A gentile can nullify his own idol,
and that of his fellow,
phrases.notes: "His fellow" means another gentile.

phrases.english: but a Jew cannot nullify
the idol of a gentile.
One who nullifies an idol nullifies its accessories;
if he nullified its accessories,
the accessories are permitted, but it remains forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: נׇכְרִי מְבַטֵּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ, וְשֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a נכרי can nullify an idol, his own or another נכרי's. Nullifying the idol frees its accessories, but nullifying the accessories alone does not free the idol.

steps.title: Two versions of the משנה taught by רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי taught his son רבי שמעון the version 'his own and his fellow's.' רבי שמעון reminded him that in his youth he had taught 'his own and a Jew's.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי taught רבי שמעון his son: A gentile can nullify his own idol and his fellow's. He said to him: רבי, in your youth you taught us: A gentile can nullify his own idol and a Jew's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה was taught in two versions by the same teacher. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later version says a נכרי can nullify another נכרי's idol. The earlier version said a נכרי can nullify a Jew's idol. That earlier version is surprising, and the גמרא will now question it.

keyTerms.meaning: You taught us (a version of the משנה)
In your youth, when you were younger

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi taught
Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi:

phrases.aramaic: נׇכְרִי מְבַטֵּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ וְשֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: A gentile can nullify his own idol and that of his fellow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, שָׁנִיתָ לָנוּ בְּיַלְדוּתֶךָ
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi, you taught us in your youth

phrases.aramaic: נׇכְרִי מְבַטֵּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ וְשֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: A gentile can nullify his own idol and that of a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents two versions of the משנה from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an earlier version of the משנה in which a נכרי can nullify a Jew's idol.

steps.title: How can a Jew's idol ever be nullified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier version: the פסוק 'וְשָׂם בַּסֵּתֶר' shows that a Jew's idol can never be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a Jew's idol be nullified? But it is written: 'And he shall set it up in a hidden place'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier version of the משנה using a פסוק about a Jew's idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a Jew who makes an idol. The גמרא understands it to mean that such an idol stays forbidden permanently and cannot be nullified. So how could a נכרי nullify it?

keyTerms.meaning: Can it really be nullified? (asked as a challenge)
'And he shall set it up in a hidden place,' a פסוק about a Jew's idol

phrases.english: Can that of a Jew be nullified?
But it is written: "And he shall set it up in a hidden place"!
phrases.notes: דברים 27:15. This פסוק is about a Jew's idol, and the גמרא reads it as staying forbidden for good.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִי קָא מְבַטְּלָהּ? וְהָא ״וְשָׂם בַּסָּתֶר״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier version quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version: a נכרי can nullify a Jew's idol
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows a Jew's idol can never be nullified, so the earlier version seems to contradict the פסוק.

steps.title: The case is an idol owned in partnership
steps.stepSummary: רבי הילל בריה דרבי וולס answers that the earlier version is talking about an idol that a נכרי and a Jew own together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הילל son of רבי וולס said: It is needed only where he has a partnership in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי הילל answers the challenge by limiting the earlier version to a jointly owned idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew's idol that belongs only to him can never be nullified. But when a נכרי is a partner in it, his nullifying might cover the Jew's share too. That is the case the earlier version had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this case): narrowing a ruling to a specific case

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי הִילֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי וָולֶס:
phrases.english: Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Volas, said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ שׁוּתָּפוּת.
phrases.english: It is needed only where he has a partnership in it.
phrases.notes: "He" is the gentile: he and the Jew own the idol together.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ שׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier version means any Jew's idol, which goes against the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only an idol shared by a נכרי and a Jew.

steps.title: What was רבי's reasoning in youth and in old age?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי held when he taught each version.
steps.simpleTranslation: In his youth, what did he hold? And in his old age, what did he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both versions talk about a partnership idol, the גמרא asks what reasoning stands behind each one. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions now agree on the case, a shared idol. So the change must come from a different view about how the Jewish partner worships.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he hold? What was his reasoning?

phrases.english: In his youth, what did he hold,
and in his old age, what did he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ מַאי קָסָבַר, וּבְזִקְנוּתוֹ מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the partnership answer of step 20 and asks for the reasoning behind each version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי's earlier and later versions of the משנה.

steps.title: Does the Jew worship on the gentile's intention or his own?
steps.stepSummary: In his youth, רבי held that the Jew worships based on the נכרי's intention, so the נכרי's nullification frees the Jew's share too. In his old age, he held that the Jew worships on his own intention, so only the נכרי's share is freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In his youth he held: the Jew worships based on the gentile's intention, so once the gentile nullifies his own share, the Jew's share is nullified too. In his old age he held: the Jew worships based on his own intention, so when the gentile nullifies his own share, the Jew's share is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי changed his mind about whose intention drives the Jewish partner's worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Jew is just following the נכרי, then the idol's status depends on the נכרי, and his nullification covers everything. If the Jew worships on his own, his share has its own forbidden status. A Jew's idol can never be nullified, so his share stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי's later view, which matches our משנה, is that a Jewish partner worships on his own intention. So a נכרי can nullify only his own share, and the Jew's share stays forbidden.

phrases.english: In his youth he held:
the Jew worships based on the gentile's intention;
since the gentile nullifies his own,
that of the Jew is nullified as well.
And in his old age he held:
the Jew worships based on his own intention;
when the gentile nullifies, it is his own share,
but that of the Jew is not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ סָבַר: יִשְׂרָאֵל אַדַּעְתָּא דְּנׇכְרִי פָּלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two versions depend on whether the Jewish partner worships on the נכרי's intention (youth) or on his own intention (old age).

steps.title: Some teach רבי הילל's statement on the last clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second version. In it, רבי הילל's statement is attached to the סיפא of the משנה: a Jew cannot nullify a נכרי's idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach this statement as referring to the last clause of the משנה: 'A Jew cannot nullify the עבודה זרה of a נכרי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is switching to a second version of where רבי הילל's teaching belongs. It is setting up a question on the last line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי הילל used his teaching to answer a question about רבי's early wording. Here, the same teaching is attached to the סיפא instead. The סיפא says a Jew's act of nullifying does nothing to a נכרי's idol. This step only quotes that line, so the גמרא can question it next.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a different version)
The last clause of the משנה
Nullifies, cancels an object's status as an idol
An idol, an object of idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new teacher or a new idea. It is the same statement of רבי הילל, simply attached to a different line of the משנה.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the last clause:
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי הילל's statement from earlier. This version attaches it to the last line of the משנה.

phrases.english: A Jew cannot nullify
the idol of a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of where רבי הילל's teaching from step 20 belongs, attaching it to the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סיפא of the משנה states: a Jew cannot nullify a נכרי's idol.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that a Jew cannot nullify a נכרי's idol, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the סיפא. Why would the משנה bother to teach something so plain?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew has no ownership or say over a נכרי's idol. So it seems clear that his nullifying it would do nothing. The גמרא assumes every line of a משנה teaches something new, so it asks what this line adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Used to ask why a source bothers to state something simple.
Nullification, removing an object's status as an idol

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the סיפא that was just quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סיפא: a Jew cannot nullify a נכרי's idol.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems self-evident, so it should not need to be stated. Every line of a משנה is expected to teach something new.

steps.title: רבי הילל begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי הילל בריה דרבי וולס begins to answer why the סיפא is needed. His answer continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הילל, son of [רבי וולס], said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces רבי הילל as the one who will answer the 'it's obvious' question. Only the opening of his answer appears here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line sets up the answer. In this version, רבי הילל's teaching is what explains why the סיפא is not obvious. His actual words continue right after this point.

phrases.english: Said Rabbi Hillel, son of
phrases.notes: The name continues: 'בריה דרבי וולס,' the same רבי הילל from step 20. His answer comes right after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the 'it's obvious' challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answer begins here and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא seemed to teach something obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated. רבי הילל's explanation continues on the next עמוד.
